ast.scope: Child source-bound partial syntax; no composed semantic AST.

obernants.assumptions: No corpus, network, teacher, GPU, held-out evaluation or model mutation. No assurance for malformed serialized models/blobs, huge counters, allocation/I/O fault injection, cyclic tree paths. Build-time dictionary generation not semantically revalidated by temp output fixture.
obernants.domain: Bounded UTF-8 synthetic fixtures, frozen generated dictionary from repository build inputs; valid index domains and aligned arrays. Tagging nonempty sequences requires supported candidate paths; tree conjunction ancestry must terminate. Tiny in-memory training only; lexgen tempfile effects.
obernants.observation_scope: Tag and ptag call dict/hash/gram; ptag uses TnT prior only unknown words. Morph's UD/AGID/rule priority interacts with lexgen src flags and record order: changing a/r/u alters preferred analyses. tok spacing bits are not exact whitespace; consumers cannot infer original byte offsets from detokenize. text order is 1-based while array positions and dictionary indexes are 0-based. udreg validates selected enum features, so upstream Feats::parse unknown-dropping cannot become a complete annotation gate. Existing conllu callers supply Sentence/Token to learning/generation.
obernants.operator: Composition excludes exact raw-whitespace recovery, unknown-feature validation after lossy parse, and transactional two-file generation. Hash equality cannot establish lexical identity; dict must compare bytes. Beam output cannot be claimed a global Viterbi optimum.

obernants.operator: Compatible antecedents for output tags include all lexical/model states attaining chosen score/order; they are many-valued. Morph codec restores exact original form via case/Raw witness, but lemmas alone do not invert forms. Tokenized rendering has arbitrary whitespace antecedents. TSV artifacts reconstruct IDs only with old-heap/order provenance.
